label: Missed verdict: a profile fails to favour what its standard ranks higher
term: missed verdict of a standard (MissesVerdict std φ)
definition: MissesVerdict std φ, for a standard std and a favouring profile φ (each a ranking of candidates in each variation scenario): for some scenario s and candidates x, y, the standard ranks x over y at s and φ does not favour x over y at s. With std the value ranking (DEF 071b24f0), the profile fails to favour something that is better. It measures the profile only against the supplied standard; the same function applied with the end-realization ordering as std measures it against end content instead.
note: Stipulative analyst notion (#2145 premise lane P), attribution deferred. It is the loss half of a standard-relative reading of 'restriction of content is limitation'; see docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section 'When is a restriction of content a limitation?'. Profiles are not total rankings, so missing a verdict is not the same as favouring the opposite.
